minutes.headline: Commission approved a Laurel Lane teardown-rebuild without the tree removals and backed Rich Birch's reappointment.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard the Lake Shirley Improvement Corps annual report, then acted on a notice of intent, two continuances, a dock determination and two tree administrative determinations. Members also discussed the Northfield Road intermittent stream lesson learned, the master plan committee, appointments and the Hollis Road house. No budget figures were discussed.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved a notice of intent to demolish and rebuild at 68 Laurel Lane, without approving tree removal between 30 and 50 feet.
Trees at 68 Laurel Lane are to come back later as a field change request after an arborist report, not in this approval.
The commission voted to have the chair write a letter recommending Richard Birch's reappointment.
Tree removals were approved at 17 Horizon Island Road, with two native hardwoods as replacements, and at 38 Oak Ridge.
A dock at 52 Spring Street Extension got a negative determination, and the skatepark and Reservoir Road hearings were continued to June 7th.

why_it_matters: These are permit decisions on land near wetlands and water, so they decide what a homeowner may build or cut near protected resource areas, not what a resident pays in taxes.
The Laurel Lane trees are still undecided, and the skatepark at 100 Chestnut Street is still before the commission, so both could return as public hearings.
watch_next: June 7th: continued hearings for the Lunenburg Skatepark at 100 Chestnut Street and the Payne project at 647 Reservoir Road.
A field change request for the tree work at 68 Laurel Lane, after the arborist report.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on all eight votes and their outcomes, and the differences are mostly misheard names. The one substantive difference is the Northfield Road case: ours records no changes to bylaws or regulations and a plan to study intermittent streams and soil samples, while the official minutes record a lesson about looking for vernal pools.
